title: Crack a code with a stated key

sections.skill: Decode and encode with a stated key, and find a key within a stated family

questions.prompt: In a code, each letter has the value of its position in the alphabet (A = 1, B = 2, ..., Z = 26), and a word's value is the sum of its letters' values. For example, CAB = 3 + 1 + 2 = 6. What is the value of BEAD?
In a code, every letter is replaced by the letter 3 places later in the alphabet (A becomes D, B becomes E, and X, Y, Z wrap around to A, B, C). A coded word reads FDW. What was the original word?
A code adds the same whole number k to every digit and keeps only the last digit of each sum (so 8 + 3 gives 1). The code turns 2025 into 4247. What does it turn 1990 into?
Each symbol stands for a whole number. Star + Star = 10. Star + Circle = 8. Circle + Square = 9. What number is Square?
Two 3-letter words were interleaved: first letter of word 1, first letter of word 2, second letter of word 1, and so on. The result is CDAORT. Which two words were interleaved?

sections.skill: Strategy: write the key as a table
sections.relationship: Students who decode in their head lose track of which way the key works. Writing the key as a table and applying it one symbol at a time keeps encoding and decoding straight.
sections.author_note: Students who decode in their head lose track of which way the key works. Writing the key as a table and applying it one symbol at a time keeps encoding and decoding straight.

lesson.title: Write the key as a table
text: A code is a rule that turns each symbol into another symbol (or a number).
Write the key as a two-row table: plain symbols on top, coded symbols below. To encode, read top to bottom; to decode, find the coded symbol on the bottom row and read up.
When the key must be found from an example, use the example to fill in the table, then check the key on EVERY symbol of the example before using it.

example.title: Worked example (a different code)
prompt: A code replaces each digit d by 9 - d. What is 274 in code, and what number does the code 815 come from?
steps: Decode 815: 8 comes from 1, 1 from 8, 5 from 4, so 184.

questions.prompt: A code replaces each letter by its position in the alphabet (A = 1, ..., Z = 26) and adds them. What is the value of DOG?
A code moves each letter 1 place later (A -> B, ..., Z -> A). What is BOX in code?
A code replaces each digit d by 9 - d. What is the code for 306?
If a code moves every letter 2 places later, then decoding moves every letter 2 places earlier.
Triangle + Triangle + Triangle = 12. What number is Triangle?

sections.skill: Codes with structure: shapes of letters and combined rules
sections.relationship: Harder: a key based on letter shapes, and two rules applied in order.
sections.label: ADVANCED APPLICATION

questions.prompt: In this code, a letter's value is the number of closed spaces inside it in plain block capitals: A, D, O, P, Q and R have 1, B has 2, and every other letter has 0. A word's value is the sum of its letters' values. What is the value of BREAD?

In this code, a letter's value is the number of closed spaces inside it in plain block capitals: A, D, O, P, Q and R have 1, B has 2, and every other letter has 0. A word's value is the sum of its letters' values. Which word has value 0?
A code first writes a word backward and then moves each letter 1 place later in the alphabet. What is the code for MAP?
Each symbol stands for a whole number. Moon + Moon + Sun = 13. Sun + Sun = 6. Moon + Star = 9. What number is Star?
A code moves every letter 13 places later in the alphabet (wrapping around). Applying this code twice gives back the original word.

sections.skill: Find a key and prove when none exists
sections.relationship: Expert: determine a key from coded examples, and show that a requested code cannot exist.
sections.label: EXPERT CHALLENGE

questions.prompt: A code adds 3 to each digit of a 4-digit number and keeps only the last digit of each sum (so 8 becomes 1). Is there a 4-digit number whose code is the same number written backward?

choices.text: No: but only because the first digit cannot be 0.
No: the middle digits would need b + 6 to end in the same digit as b, which never happens.
Yes: any number whose digits are all equal works.

questions.correct_answer: No: the middle digits would need b + 6 to end in the same digit as b, which never happens.

questions.prompt: A code moves every letter the same number of places later in the alphabet (wrapping around). It turns GO into MU. What does it turn LOGIC into?
Each symbol stands for a whole number from 1 to 9. Square + Square = Circle, and Circle + Square = 12. Find Square s and Circle c.
questions.rule: (s + s == c and c + s == 12 and isInteger(s) and isInteger(c)) and isInteger(s) and s >= 1 and isInteger(c) and c >= 1
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: (s + s == c and c + s == 12 and isInteger(s) and isInteger(c)) and isInteger(s) and s >= 1 and isInteger(c) and c >= 1 (example: s = 4, c = 8)

questions.prompt: In this code, a letter's value is the number of closed spaces inside it in plain block capitals: A, D, O, P, Q and R have 1, B has 2, and every other letter has 0. A word's value is the sum of its letters' values. Using only the letters B, O and T (each as often as you like), what is the greatest value of a 4-letter string?
A code sends each letter to the letter at the same distance from the other end of the alphabet (A <-> Z, B <-> Y, C <-> X, ...). Which word is coded as itself?

choices.text: No word: no letter is coded as itself.

questions.correct_answer: No word: no letter is coded as itself.
